title: Town Elder
dialogue: Welcome to Hearthvale, traveler. The vale keeps its warmth even in hard years.
When you reach your stride, carry a letter for me to Millwick Crossing.
The fountain behind me has run since my grandmother’s day. Make a wish, if you like.
dialogue.title: Vale Elder
dialogue: Welcome to Hearthlight Vale, traveler. The lanterns burn brighter now that you are here.
Old Millwick has gone quiet, and I fear a letter of mine never reached him.
When your legs are steady — say, level eight — come back and I will ask a favor of you.

dialogue.title: General Goods
dialogue: Fresh goods straight from the vale roads. Care to browse the stall?
Potions, rope, a lantern for the mine — I stock what a wanderer needs.
Buy low in town, sell high on the road. That’s the whole trick.
Potions, rope, a lantern or two — everything a green adventurer forgets to pack.
Coin up front, and I will not ask where the monsters found it.

dialogue.title: Warp Attendant
dialogue: Need to travel far? The Hearth network can spare you the walk — for a fee.
I can only send you where a warp stone still burns. Unlock more as you explore.
dialogue.title: Warp Keeper
dialogue: Need to be somewhere yesterday? The hearth-lines run to every town that will have me.
Step onto the glow and I will fold the road beneath your feet — for a modest fee.

dialogue.title: The Warm Hearth Inn
dialogue: Rooms are warm and the stew is hot. Rest here and your wounds mend faster.
Plenty of stories drift through my common room. Stay awhile and listen.
dialogue.title: Innkeeper
dialogue: A warm bed and warmer stew — the Hearthlight Inn never turns a tired soul away.
Rest here and the road will feel kinder in the morning, I promise you that.

dialogue.title: Combat Instructor
dialogue: Grab a stance and hit the dummies. Footwork first, swagger later.
Clear your First Hunt and I’ll show you a trick or two.
Stamina wins fights as often as steel. Watch your green bar.
dialogue.title: Combat Trainer
dialogue: Grip loose, weight low, eyes on the whole field — that is how you live past level one.
Bring me proof of your first honest hunt and I will teach you a thing or two.

dialogue.title: Field Apothecary
dialogue: Clover salve and spore tonics — the plains provide, if you know where to look.
dialogue.title: Herbalist
dialogue: Cloverleaf salve, mushroom tonic, a pinch of moonpetal — I stock what the fields give up.
Fresh cuttings today. The plains have been generous since the rains.

dialogue.title: Plains Scout
dialogue: Keep low in the tall clover. The jellybuds bounce harder than they look.
dialogue.title: Field Scout
dialogue: Keep low in the clover — the plains look calm until something with teeth disagrees.
I have been mapping the far hedgerows. Could use sharp eyes out there before long.

dialogue.title: Spore Researcher
dialogue: Every mushroom here has a temper. Bring me caps and I’ll pay in coin and lore.
dialogue.title: Mycologist
dialogue: The Hollow breathes, you know — spores in, spores out, all day and night.
Some caps glow, some bite back. I could use a runner to gather the harmless sort.

dialogue.title: Whisperwood Warden
dialogue: The wood whispers to those who tread softly. Loud boots draw the barklings.
dialogue.title: Whisperwood Ranger
dialogue: The Whisperwood remembers every footstep. Tread it with respect.
Something has been thinning the deer trails. Walk with me and we may learn what.

dialogue.title: Road Miller
dialogue: Wind’s been fickle, so the mill’s been slow. Mind the roadjacks past the verge.
dialogue.title: Miller
dialogue: Wheel turns, stone grinds, flour flies — same song every day and I love it still.
Mind the sacks by the door. Trip over one and the whole town hears about it.

dialogue.title: Hired Blade
dialogue: Move along the road and you’ll be fine. Stray off it and you’re on your own.
dialogue.title: Caravan Guard
dialogue: Eyes open, blade oiled. The road pays best to those who reach the end of it.
We roll for the riverside town come dawn. Long haul, but the ale is worth it.

dialogue.title: Millwick Mayor
dialogue: Millwick welcomes honest travelers. Trouble at the moonwell, though — ask around.
dialogue.title: Town Mayor
dialogue: Riverside welcomes you. Keep your boots dry and your temper drier.
The docks have troubles I would rather solve quietly. Perhaps you are the quiet sort.

dialogue.title: Riverside Trader
dialogue: River trade brings the finest wares upstream. Take a look before you cross.
Goods off the barges, fresh as the tide — I undercut the town square and sleep fine for it.
Haggle if you like, but my prices already float lower than most.

dialogue.title: Crystal Prospector
dialogue: The vein runs deep and mean. Bring me shards and I’ll mark the safe ledges.
dialogue.title: Prospector
dialogue: These foothills are lousy with crystal, if you know where the seams hide.
My last dig ran into something that dug back. Might pay a brave soul to have a look.

dialogue.title: Moonwell Watcher
dialogue: The moonwell stirs. Recover its sigil before the wraiths finish what they started.

dialogue.title: Gate Watch
dialogue: The east gate stays open, but the plains beyond do not forgive the careless.
Keep your blade sheathed in town. Outside the wall is another matter.

dialogue.title: Hearthstone Bakery
dialogue: Honey rolls, fresh from the stone. A warm loaf mends more than you’d think.
Take one for the road — the plains are hungry work.

dialogue.title: Wandering Minstrel
dialogue: A coin for a song? I know the ballad of the Moonwell, if your heart is brave.
They say every hero of the vale started right here, by this fountain.

dialogue.title: Vale Child
dialogue: Are you a real adventurer? Can I see your sword? Pleeease?
I’m gonna be a ranger someday, just like Elowen in the woods!

dialogue.title: Keeper of the Hearth
dialogue: May the hearthlight keep you. Rest in the vale and let its calm settle your spirit.
Dark things stir beyond Millwick. When you are ready, the vale will ask much of you.
The Moonwell only opens to those it deems ready. Patience, wanderer.
Bring me the sigil the glade keeps hidden — near level ten, when your spirit can bear it.
